title: ERV-1 — Expanded Report View Delivery
summary: rehost an explicitly eligible live report in the full-width Content Detail view and add temporary Manage-only widths to Catalogue Works
content_html:
ERV-1 — Expanded Report View Delivery

Status And Purpose

ERV-1.1 is complete. ERV-1.1R is now defined as the corrective checkpoint that removes unused public composition while retaining the public-safe implementation and Manage composition. This update changes delivery documentation only; no report opts in, no manual widths exist, and ERV-1 is parked before ERV-1.1R implementation approval.

ERV-1 delivers the first complete Expanded Report View outcome: an explicitly eligible live report can open in the existing full-width Content Detail layout without cloning, remounting, or losing report-owned state. Manage additionally gives an eligible semantic table temporary accessible column widths. The local catalogue_works report is the sole product adoption in this delivery.

Complete Outcome

  • A report or preset opts in only through an explicit successful module-mount result. Registry metadata, rendered width, overflow, row count, headings, and DOM shape never grant eligibility.
  • The open control appears only after the exact report has mounted successfully and its presentation result has passed validation.
  • Content Detail moves the exact live report root into one bounded full-width viewport. Search, sorting, current rows, report actions, event listeners, and route-owned state remain on the same DOM and report instance.
  • Back to document restores the root to its exact authored host position, restores page scroll and invocation focus, and keeps the report state. Document navigation releases the expanded target without restoring stale content.
  • The adapter remains public-safe in its site-owned shared module, but only Manage composes it until a named public report adopts it. Public routes download neither the adapter module nor its control and viewport selectors merely because the implementation is public-safe.
  • Manage can resize only a presentation that declares one exact semantic table and an ordered stable column model. Pointer and keyboard resizing use one managed colgroup; Reset widths returns to the report's natural responsive table.
  • Widths exist only for the active expanded presentation. They are not written to source, registry JSON, URLs, browser storage, canonical data, or generated payloads.
  • Widening columns produces horizontal scrolling inside the expanded viewport. The ordinary embedded report retains its current fit-and-reflow presentation.

Selected Capability Contract

Eligibility is code-owned by the mounted report module rather than added to reports.json. A successful eligible mount resolves with this focused browser handle:

{
  expandedPresentation: {
    kind: "flow" | "semantic-table",
    label: "Catalogue Works",
    table: tableNode,
    columns: [
      { id: "work", label: "Work" },
      { id: "year", label: "Year" }
    ],
    subscribe: subscribePresentationRefresh
  }
}

flow opts the exact live report root into shared expansion and omits table, columns, and subscribe. semantic-table additionally supplies the exact table, a non-empty ordered immutable column-id/label model, and a subscription that notifies the presentation adapter after any header or row reconstruction. The subscription returns its cleanup callback.

The report controller already owns the exact generated report host and normalized report descriptor. After a module mount resolves, it validates this optional handle and registers it with the entrypoint-supplied report-presentation adapter. An absent or invalid handle leaves the successfully mounted report embedded and undecorated; it does not infer a fallback presentation.

The exact expanded target freezes:

  • host document identity {viewer scope, doc_id};
  • document-mount generation;
  • report id;
  • report descriptor scope, preset, and sub-scope values; and
  • the one registered live root.

There is no report-instance id because a document has at most one Report Block. Selected rows, visible labels, current route alone, and the first matching report are never identity inputs.

catalogue_works returns kind: "semantic-table" only after its canonical inputs and first complete render succeed. Its existing COLUMN_KEYS and labels become the one ordered column model used by header cells, body cells, sorting, TSV export, and widths. The report notifies after its current header/body rerender. The shared adapter does not learn Catalogue fields or report-specific state.

Delivery Boundary

ERV-1 includes:

  • one shared report-presentation adapter and open-control lifecycle;
  • explicit Manage composition through the existing Content Detail view, with public composition deferred until a named public report adoption;
  • exact live-root rehosting, placeholder restoration, Back/navigation release, scroll/focus restoration, and stale-target rejection;
  • one shared bounded expanded-report viewport with horizontal scrolling;
  • one Manage-only semantic-table width extension reusing the current managed-table sizing seam;
  • catalogue_works presentation-handle and stable-column adoption;
  • focused shared, public-boundary, Manage-width, and Catalogue Works module evidence; and
  • concise durable transfer to Reports, Report Capability and Composition, and Catalogue Works at closeout.

ERV-1 excludes:

  • cloning, a second report mount, refetching report data, or a parallel report-state owner;
  • adding eligibility or column configuration to source Report Blocks, report registry JSON, generated document payloads, or public registry projection;
  • applying the Markdown Table detail marker or clone adapter to reports;
  • adding Copy table to Content Detail for reports; catalogue_works keeps its report-owned Copy action inside the moved live root;
  • persisted or URL-owned widths, saved views, user-defined columns, or an editor for report layout;
  • resizing in the ordinary embedded report;
  • a generic report plugin, dashboard, presentation registry, DOM scanner, or geometry/overflow observer;
  • converting another report to semantic table markup;
  • project_state, works, docs_subscope, public report, or composite sub-scope-customisation adoption; and
  • a tabular CSS Grid width projector before an accepted report requires one.

Current Owners To Inspect

ERV-1.0 starts at these existing seams and narrows the exact changed set before implementation:

  • site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-content-detail-view.js, the view coordinator, document controller, app runtime, and public entrypoint for exact target, expanded layout, Back, and document-navigation lifecycle;
  • docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/docs-viewer-reports.js and site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/docs-viewer-public-reports.js for successful module-mount result handling and the separate local/public executable allowlists;
  • the Manage and public document-extras entrypoints for explicit adapter composition without moving report ownership into the shared document controller;
  • docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-managed-table-tools.js for the current colgroup, pointer, keyboard, Reset widths, and control-projection primitives while retaining existing Markdown Table Detail behavior;
  • docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/catalogue-works-report.js and docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-local-reports.css for the sole adoption, stable column ids, rerender notification, and unchanged embedded layout;
  • site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-reports.css, site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer.css, and docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-manage.css for shared report viewport, existing Content Detail layout, and Manage-only handles; and
  • the current Table Detail, Catalogue Works, public runtime-boundary, route-navigation, and report-module tests.

This is an inspection route, not a frozen file inventory. Stop and re-scope if the result needs report registry schema changes, generated payload changes, a second mount, a general presentation engine, a public management import, a second width owner, or broad report rewrites.

Delivery Steps

ERV-1.0 — Confirm Capability And Implementation Fit

  • [x] Trace the current document-render, asynchronous report-mount, Content Detail, Back, and navigation-release order in public and Manage entrypoints.
  • [x] Validate the selected expandedPresentation mount-result shape against both report controllers, preset context, stale asynchronous mounts, and catalogue_works header/body rerendering.
  • [x] Freeze exact control placement, target identity, placeholder/restoration behavior, focus/scroll behavior, unavailable behavior, and the boundary between shared expansion and Manage-only widths.
  • [x] Confirm how the current managed-table width primitive can serve the live semantic table while Table Detail retains its cloned-table Copy and Reset behavior.
  • [x] Name the exact production files, focused tests, expected CSS owners, rough production/test diff, main risks, and rollback boundary.

Checkpoint: record one concise ERV-1.0 sanity result with exact files, reused seams, mount-result validation, lifecycle ordering, diff estimate, risks, and unresolved decisions. Stop before ERV-1.1 implementation approval.

ERV-1.0 Sanity Record

ERV-1 fits the current runtime without changing Report Block source, registry metadata, generated payloads, services, report data, or route state. The selected optional module-mount result is the only new capability declaration. No unresolved design decision remains.

Current lifecycle and reused seams. The shared document controller assigns a positive mount generation, renders the exact payload host, mounts Table and Diagram adapters synchronously, then starts report mounting through the asynchronous document-extras hook. Both local and public report controllers validate one generated host, registry access, and one allowlisted loader, but currently discard the module's resolved value. The extras path already receives the document generation; ERV-1.1 needs only to pass that generation, requestContentDetail, and the entrypoint-supplied report adapter through the existing public/Manage report calls.

Back already requests rendered-document with reason back. Route loading, payload replacement, missing-document state, Search, and Recent leave Content Detail through reason document-navigation; the hosted-view unmount runs synchronously before the accepted render callback changes or hides document content. ERV-1.1 therefore adds one explicit report-adapter release at the current pane-hide, loading, replacement, and status boundaries beside their existing presentation releases. A late module result must repeat the existing host-current check after its promise resolves and cannot register a control for a detached root or newer mount generation.

Content Detail currently captures scroll after calling an adapter. That is safe for cloned Table and Diagram presentations but too late for a live-root move, which can change document geometry. ERV-1.1 captures scroll before mountPresentation, passes the release reason to the presentation, restores the report only on Back or a same-document presentation failure, and releases without restoring stale report content on document-navigation. Existing Table and Diagram presentations ignore the added release context and retain their behavior.

Frozen capability and target. A module opts in only by resolving a successful mount with own property expandedPresentation. flow requires one visible label and no table fields. semantic-table additionally requires one exact descendant TABLE, a non-empty ordered unique list of {id, label}, and subscribe(listener), which returns one cleanup callback. Headers and every current body row use the same ordered data-report-column-id values with no row or column spans; a table that cannot meet that contract can still declare flow but receives no widths.

An absent handle is ordinary and produces no warning or control. An invalid explicit handle leaves the successfully mounted report embedded and undecorated and emits one development warning; it never replaces the report with an unavailable state. The post-mount control is inserted immediately before the exact generated root and requests target kind report with immutable {viewer scope, doc_id}, document generation, report id, and descriptor scope/preset/sub-scope. The control label is Open [report label] in expanded view. No selected row, displayed text, current route alone, or instance fallback participates.

The shared adapter stores one registration per document content root. Opening inserts one exact placeholder before the report root, moves that same root into a focusable docsViewerReport__expandedViewport, and exposes no new-tab target. Back moves the root before the placeholder, removes the placeholder and expanded section, restores the captured scroll, and focuses the still-connected invocation control. Navigation removes the expanded section/root and then releases the registration, control, and any active subscription exactly once.

Managed widths and Catalogue Works. The current Manage table owner already supplies pointer capture, Left/Right keyboard steps, measured widths, one direct colgroup, Reset, release cleanup, and shared Content Detail control projection. It currently snapshots one header row once and always exposes its own Copy control. catalogue_works reconstructs its header on every search and sort render, so direct reuse without a refresh path would orphan resize handles.

ERV-1.2 keeps one sizing owner and adds a report presentation extension to it. The extension validates the declared ids against current headers and rows, hides the Content Detail Copy control, subscribes only while the report is expanded, removes old handles and binds current headers after a notified rerender, and retains the existing colgroup widths while exact correspondence remains valid. A mismatch clears widths and handles and fails closed. The existing Table Detail extension keeps inferred simple-header eligibility for its accepted static clone plus its current Reset and Copy controls.

catalogue_works reuses its current COLUMN_KEYS and labels for the five-column handle, writes data-report-column-id on each header/body cell, owns a small listener set, and notifies after renderCurrent. The initial empty-search table may remain hidden; entering search reveals the same table, and the notification binds/measures its current headers. A successful data load and first render return the capability. Failed or invalid input retains its existing contained report state and returns no capability. Search, sorting, links, counts, and report-owned TSV Copy remain unchanged.

Exact proposed change set. ERV-1.1 adds site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-report-presentation.js; registers it in site-tools/config/site-tools.json; and updates the shared Content Detail, document controller, app boot/runtime, public entry/report entry/report controller, Manage entry/report entry/report controller, and shared reports stylesheet. Focused evidence adds docs-viewer/tests/smoke/docs_viewer_expanded_report_modules.py, extends test_docs_viewer_public_runtime_boundaries.py, and registers the new smoke in admin-app/commands/run_checks.py. Existing Table and Diagram smokes remain regression evidence. Expect roughly 320–440 production/config lines and 320–460 focused test/profile lines.

ERV-1.2 updates docs-viewer-managed-table-tools.js, docs-viewer-manage.js, catalogue-works-report.js, and the Manage stylesheet. It extends the expanded-report, Table Detail, and Catalogue Works module smokes plus the focused Catalogue Works contract only where static ownership evidence is useful. No local-report CSS change is expected unless real expanded presentation proves one narrowly scoped natural-width correction. Expect roughly 150–240 production/CSS lines and 220–360 focused test lines. The complete delivery is therefore expected to remain near 470–680 production/config lines and 540–820 test/profile lines without a schema, service, registry, or general presentation framework.

Focused evidence and baseline. ERV-1.0 baseline passed the existing Table Detail module smoke, Catalogue Works module smoke, and 17 public-runtime/Catalogue Works Python contracts. The first sandboxed Python attempt stopped during collection because the configured external-local workspace was not writable to the sandbox; the identical focused set passed with the configured workspace available. Implementation checkpoints use changed-file JavaScript lint, the new expanded-report smoke, existing Table/Diagram/Catalogue Works smokes in proportion to changed seams, the two focused Python owners, bin/site-validate after adding the public shared module, Studio docs/search builds for evidence updates, generated JSON parsing, the public static-import assertion, and git diff --check. ERV-1.3 runs the maintained docs-viewer-smoke profile after the new command is registered.

Risks and rollback. The material risks are capturing scroll after the live move, registering a late detached root, restoring stale content during navigation, orphaning handles after a header rebuild, leaking the Table Detail Copy control into a report, accepting mismatched column ids, and omitting the new shared module from the public runtime manifest. Each has one owner and focused assertion above. ERV-1.1 rolls back by removing the new adapter and context threading; ERV-1.2 rolls back the optional Catalogue Works result and refresh-aware extension. Neither checkpoint migrates source, data, configuration schema, or user state, and no compatibility reader or dual path is required.

ERV-1.0 review gate: implementation fit is confirmed and no product code has changed. Stop before ERV-1.1 until its shared live-report foundation is explicitly approved.

ERV-1.1 — Add Shared Live-Report Expansion

  • [x] Add the shared report-presentation adapter and explicitly compose the same public-safe adapter into public and Manage Content Detail definitions.
  • [x] Let each separate report controller register only a validated expandedPresentation result from the exact successfully mounted module.
  • [x] Add the post-mount open control and immutable target without deriving identity or eligibility from rendered content.
  • [x] Rehost the one live report root inside a bounded expanded viewport, retain one exact restoration marker, and preserve the module's listeners and state.
  • [x] Restore on Back; release without stale restoration on navigation, failed remount, or adapter disposal; remove controls and subscriptions exactly once.
  • [x] Add shared CSS for the expanded report viewport and horizontal containment without changing ordinary embedded report layouts.
  • [x] Prove public/Manage composition, post-mount eligibility, no clone/remount/refetch, state retention, stale-target rejection, restoration, and absence of management imports on public routes.

Checkpoint: focused module and route evidence passes for the shared live-root lifecycle and public boundary. No report has manual widths yet. Stop before ERV-1.2 approval.

ERV-1.1 Implementation Record

Shared capability owner. site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-report-presentation.js now validates only an explicit own expandedPresentation result, creates the exact post-mount control and frozen document/report target, moves the one registered live root through a restoration comment into the shared expanded viewport, and distinguishes Back or view-failure restoration from document-navigation disposal. An absent result is ordinary; an invalid explicit result warns and leaves the mounted report embedded.

Composition and lifecycle. Public and Manage each create the same shared adapter and pass it explicitly through app boot/runtime, Content Detail, the document controller, their separate document-extras entrypoint, and their separate report controller. Each report controller preserves the successful module result, repeats the exact host-current check after the asynchronous mount, and delegates optional registration without changing report availability. Content Detail captures scroll before the live move and passes the release reason. The document controller releases report registration at the existing pane-hide, loading, payload-replacement, and status boundaries.

Presentation and public boundary. docs-viewer-reports.css owns the control and bounded focusable viewport; ordinary embedded report layout selectors are unchanged. The new shared module is registered in the public runtime manifest. Public static imports remain management-free, and Manage supplies no width extension in this checkpoint.

Focused evidence. Changed JavaScript and Python lint, Python compilation, git diff --check, and bin/site-validate passed. docs_viewer_expanded_report_modules.py passed exact optional eligibility, immutable identity, live-node/state/listener retention, Back restoration, navigation disposal, stale rejection, pre-move scroll capture, document-lifecycle release, and public/Manage composition. Existing Table Detail and Diagram Detail module smokes passed. The focused public-runtime boundary file passed 12 tests; the initial sandboxed collection stopped because the configured external-local workspace was not writable, and the identical test passed with that configured workspace available.

Diff boundary. The implementation is approximately 505 added production/config/CSS lines and 501 added focused test/profile lines, slightly above the rough ERV-1.0 estimate because the adapter validates both presentation kinds and the new smoke covers the lifecycle without borrowing a product report. It remains one bounded adapter and one focused smoke: no report module, Report Block, registry, generated document payload, service, schema, route, managed sizing owner, or ordinary report stylesheet changed.

ERV-1.1 review gate: the shared live-report foundation is complete and verified. No current report returns the capability, so no product UI control appears yet. ERV-1.1R now owns the required public-composition correction; stop before its implementation until explicitly approved.

ERV-1.1R — Remove Unused Public Composition

  • [x] Keep site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-report-presentation.js public-safe and registered in the site runtime manifest without treating public addressability or manifest inventory as browser composition.
  • [x] Keep the generic shared adapter injection and lifecycle seams required by Manage, and keep Manage importing, constructing, supplying, and releasing the exact shared adapter.
  • [x] Remove the adapter import, construction, and Content Detail wiring from the public entrypoint so it is absent from the public transitive import graph.
  • [x] Remove expanded-presentation context and successful-mount registration from the public document-extras and public report-controller path; a future public adopter restores those edges explicitly.
  • [x] Move the report expansion control and viewport selectors out of the public-loaded shared report stylesheet and into the local report stylesheet loaded by Manage.
  • [x] Reverse the public-boundary and expanded-report composition assertions so they require Manage composition, public non-composition, and unchanged shared live-root behavior.
  • [x] Prove public routes download neither the adapter module nor its selectors, while Manage retains the exact public-safe implementation and no report adoption or width behavior begins.

Checkpoint: focused import-graph, stylesheet-owner, module-lifecycle, lint, site-validation, and generated-document evidence passes for Manage-only composition. Stop before ERV-1.2 approval.

ERV-1.1R Implementation Record

Retained public-safe owner. site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-report-presentation.js is unchanged and remains present in the site runtime manifest. The generic optional adapter injection in shared app boot/runtime, Content Detail, and the document controller is also unchanged. Manage still imports, constructs, supplies, registers, and releases that exact adapter; public supplies no adapter, so the shared injection seam is not public composition.

Corrected public graph. The public entrypoint no longer imports or constructs the report-presentation adapter and no longer supplies it to app boot or Content Detail. Public document extras no longer forward documentMountGeneration, reportPresentationAdapter, or requestContentDetail into the public report path. The public report controller still awaits a successful exact mount and rejects a stale host, but it no longer retains the mount result or contains expanded-presentation registration. A future public adopter must restore all of those edges explicitly.

Stylesheet ownership. The four expansion selector families—control row, open control/icon, and expanded viewport—moved unchanged from site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-reports.css to docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-local-reports.css. The checked public route and public-route template load only the shared report stylesheet; the Manage shell additionally loads the local report stylesheet. Ordinary shared report presentation is unchanged.

Focused evidence. JavaScript lint passed for the three changed public modules. Python lint and compilation passed for the two changed focused checks. bin/site-validate passed with 63 runtime modules, confirming that the public-safe adapter remains in the deployable runtime inventory. The expanded-report module smoke passed its retained live-root lifecycle plus reversed entrypoint/controller/stylesheet-shell composition assertions. The focused public-runtime boundary file passed 12 tests and proves the adapter is absent from the public static graph while retained by Manage and the runtime manifest. The exact selector audit reports public 0, local 4; git diff --check passes.

Diff boundary. The correction removes 30 net public production JavaScript lines and moves 63 CSS lines unchanged from the public stylesheet to the local stylesheet. Focused checks gained 55 net lines to state the negative public boundary and positive Manage/runtime-manifest ownership. No shared adapter, app boot/runtime, Content Detail, document controller, Manage production module, report implementation, Report Block, registry, payload, service, route, width owner, or visible report behavior changed.

ERV-1.1R review gate: the unused public composition is removed and focused evidence passes. No report has adopted expansion and no manual-width behavior has begun. Stop before ERV-1.2 until its Catalogue Works adoption and Manage-only sizing checkpoint is explicitly approved.

ERV-1.2 — Add Managed Widths And Adopt Catalogue Works

  • [ ] Make catalogue_works return the selected semantic-table presentation handle, apply its stable column ids to headers and cells, and notify after each current rerender.
  • [ ] Extend the Manage-only sizing composition to require exact ordered column correspondence, add accessible pointer and Left/Right keyboard handles, and rebind safely after notified rerenders.
  • [ ] Apply temporary widths through one direct colgroup, keep header and body alignment through search/sort rerenders, and contain widened output in the expanded viewport.
  • [ ] Project Reset widths only for the active resizable report, restore the natural table, and discard all overrides on Back or navigation.
  • [ ] Keep the report's existing Search, Clear, sorting, exact links, result count, and Copy table action on the same live state; add no second Content Detail copy control.
  • [ ] Prove ordinary embedded layout remains unchanged and that invalid/mismatched column models fail closed without granting resize behavior.

Checkpoint: focused Catalogue Works and managed-width evidence passes for state retention, stable columns, pointer/keyboard resizing, rerender alignment, horizontal scroll, Reset, release, and exact existing report behavior. Stop before ERV-1.3 approval.

ERV-1.3 — Verify And Transfer Durable Ownership

  • [ ] Run the focused shared/public/Manage/report module checks, changed-file JavaScript lint, warranted route smoke, docs/search rebuilds, generated JSON parsing, bounded public-import scan, and git diff --check.
  • [ ] Inspect the real local catalogue_works host through search, sort, Copy table, expand, resize, Reset, Back, re-expand, and document navigation; leave visual/tactile acceptance to the user.
  • [ ] Confirm there is one report mount, no duplicate data request, no stale root/control/subscription, no width persistence, no public expansion composition without a named adopter, no public management code, and no change to ordinary report layout.
  • [ ] Transfer the shipped current contract to Reports, Report Capability and Composition, and Catalogue Works; update Expanded Report View to the completed/deferred state.
  • [ ] Present exact implementation, verification, omission, diff-review, and documentation evidence for explicit closeout approval without adopting another report or retiring delivery material.

Checkpoint: durable owners describe the shipped result, focused evidence passes, user acceptance and closeout are recorded, and ERV-1 is complete. No delivery document is retired or deleted without separate approval.

Focused Evidence Contract

ERV-1.0 selects the exact commands. Permanent evidence should protect module-return validation, exact target/lifecycle behavior, public import separation, stable column correspondence, and report rerender integration. Visual fit, drag feel, focus feel, and mobile ergonomics remain manual checks rather than brittle permanent browser choreography.

The likely focused set is the existing Table Detail and Catalogue Works module smokes, a new narrow expanded-report module smoke, public runtime-boundary assertions, changed-file JavaScript lint, Studio docs/search builds, generated JSON parsing, and git diff --check. Existing Table Detail behavior must remain green because the Manage sizing primitive is reused rather than forked.

Acceptance

ERV-1 is complete only when the one current catalogue_works instance can move into and out of the full-width view without losing search, sort, rows, links, Copy behavior, or focus context; temporary widths remain aligned through rerenders and disappear on Reset/close; widened columns scroll only inside the expanded viewport; Manage composes the public-safe adapter; and public routes import neither the adapter nor its selectors until a named public report adopts them through a separate explicit promotion.

Deferred Work

Adopting project_state, works, public reports, docs_subscope, or collection-specific composite reports requires a separate approval after their semantic and column ownership is explicit. A tabular CSS Grid width projector, persisted layouts, saved views, optional Catalogue filters, mobile redesign, and report-specific expanded actions are not latent ERV-1 work.
